lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29-30 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out consolidates the unit vocabulary and grammar within a narrative context. Students listen to understand the story flow, then role-play the dialogue to practise natural intonation.
Look for attentive listening, correct identification of the characters’ emotions, and confident delivery of the dialogue with appropriate gestures.
“Minh and her mum are going to the farmer’s market. Shall we meet them there?”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29-30 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers checks students’ comprehension of the story details.
Look for accurate recall of the story events and correct selection of the answers corresponding to the narrative.
“What shall we buy from Minh and her grandpa?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - A Read, write, and number

details: Read, write, and number strengthens narrative comprehension and literacy skills. Students determine the correct sequence of the story frames and complete the dialogue using context clues.
Look for correct logical sequencing of the story frames and accurate completion of the sentences using the words from the box.
“Lien and her aunt will be at the market too. What shall we buy from them?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down:

Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story allows students to personalise the narrative by choosing different characters and food items. It encourages creative expression and provides communicative practice through role-play.
Look for logical choices (matching pronouns to characters), neat writing in the blanks, and enthusiastic role-play using the new story variation.
“You want to have a stand at the market, too? Ok, let’s think of what we could sell!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Listen and say focuses on phonemic awareness and pronunciation. Students listen to and repeat words with the target long 'e' sound /i:/, spelled 'ee' and 'ea', in the context of sentences.
Look for clear articulation of the long 'e' sound and accurate differentiation between the 'ee' and 'ea' spelling patterns in the target words.
“Here we are at the market! I like the look of that stall with free cheese and beef!”
